caption: Figure 2: Illustration of our hierarchical feature learning architecture and its application for set segmentation and classification using points in 2D Euclidean space as an example. Single scale point grouping is visualized here. For details on density adaptive grouping, see Fig. 3
description: This figure is a schematic representation of the PointNet++ architecture, illustrating its application in point set segmentation and classification. It shows a hierarchical feature learning process, starting with point sampling and grouping, followed by multiple levels of set abstraction using PointNet layers. The architecture includes skip links for concatenation and interpolation steps, leading to fully connected layers for classification. The figure also demonstrates the use of pointnet layers for both segmentation and classification tasks, with per-point scores and class scores as outputs. The dimensions of the data at each stage are indicated, such as (N,d+C) and (N,k).

Each method's output is shown in three separate panels, with color-coded regions representing different room elements such as walls, floors, and furniture. The "Ours" method shows a more accurate segmentation of furniture compared to PointNet.

caption: Figure 7: An example of nonrigid shape classification.
description:
## Description
This figure is a visual representation of nonrigid shape classification using PointNet++. It shows three different colored point cloud models of animals: a cat, a horse, and a giraffe. The cat is depicted in blue, the horse in yellow, and the giraffe in green. The point clouds are used to demonstrate the model's ability to classify shapes that are not perfectly aligned or in the same pose.

## Text in figure
- PointNet++
- Deep Hierarchical Feature Learning on Point Sets in a Metric Space
- Nonrigid shape classification
- Cat (blue)
- Horse (yellow)
- Giraffe (green)

caption: Figure 8: 3D point cloud patterns learned from the first layer kernels. The model is trained for ModelNet40 shape classification (20 out of the 128 kernels are randomly selected). Color indicates point depth (red is near, blue is far).
description:
Description: The figure displays 20 randomly selected 3D point cloud patterns learned from the first layer kernels of a deep learning model trained for ModelNet40 shape classification. Each pattern is represented by a colored point cloud, with color indicating point depth (red for near, blue for far). The patterns vary in shape and complexity, showcasing the model's ability to learn diverse features from point sets.

Text in figure: No text is visible in the figure. The patterns are labeled by their position in the grid, with no specific names or values provided. The color coding for point depth is indicated in the caption.

caption: Figure 9: Virtual scan generated from ScanNet
description:
## Figure Description
The figure displays two panels labeled (a) and (b), showing point cloud data from ScanNet. Panel (a) is labeled "ScanNet labeled scene" and shows a colored point cloud with distinct regions labeled in various colors. Panel (b) is labeled "ScanNet non-uniform" and shows a point cloud with less distinct color regions and more scattered points.

- Panel (a): ScanNet labeled scene
- Panel (b): ScanNet non-uniform
